exceptions.reason: Excludes only the deterministic, generated AJV standalone validator groups from human-source lint rules; contract generation enforces their exact schema inventory, runtime exports, deterministic bytes, and 600 KiB per-group ceiling.
ClaimCore.Contracts emits canonical minified JSON whose exact bytes feed the generated CLI-v4 and Web-v3 wire-contract fingerprints.

The AJV and Rolldown pipeline emits deterministic minified standalone validator groups; contract generation enforces a 600 KiB ceiling for each group and browser code dynamically imports only the typed group required by an endpoint.
Both rules conflict with the output of ruff format, which owns trailing commas and implicit string concatenation; ruff itself documents disabling them next to the formatter.
The project licence lives in the repository LICENSE file; per-file copyright headers would duplicate it and drift.
D203 and D213 are the mutually exclusive alternatives of D211 and D212; selecting every rule would demand contradictory layouts, so the conventional pair D211 and D212 stays enforced.

Every entry point and drill sets sys.dont_write_bytecode before importing its sibling modules so that running a script never writes bytecode into the checkout; that assignment must precede the imports.

Every subprocess call runs a fixed argument vector without a shell, and the listed tools (openssl, ssh, docker, PostgreSQL clients) are resolved and version-checked by the backup tooling; executing those tools is the purpose of the programs.
Drill test names state the behaviour under test and their bodies are short; a docstring would only repeat the name. Non-test modules keep every docstring rule.
Drill assertions compare against literal expected values; naming every expected literal as a constant would hide the expectation from the reader.
The drills are unittest.TestCase suites run directly by the interpreter and the repository deliberately has no pytest dependency, so the pytest-style rules do not apply to them.
Assertions are the verification mechanism of the drills and never execute in the shipped backup tooling; non-test modules keep the rule.
The prop union is checked at every call site, so the spread tuple is exactly the catalog's argument list; TypeScript cannot derive that from the generic key inside the component.
The generated catalogs are JSON modules whose ICU message shape is produced and validated by the localization generator; the inferred JSON module type is wider than the catalog map it feeds.

Draft values are built from the validated definition and a dynamic command kind, which TypeScript cannot relate to the discriminated draft union; the reducer tests and the contract corpus exercise every command kind.
The key dependency is the deliberate reload trigger: the effect must rerun when the caller's key changes even though the effect body does not read it.
The session epoch is the deliberate reload trigger: a new epoch must discard the old definition even though the effect body does not read the epoch.

Purely stylistic rules with no bug-finding value that contradict prettier's layout or each other (no-ternary against no-negated-condition, sort-keys against meaningful field order, func-style against arrow-function modules, id-length against conventional short names); every rule with correctness value stays enabled.

The rule flags every numeric literal, including exit codes, byte sizes and protocol limits that the surrounding identifier already names; the comparison-only Python equivalent (PLR2004) stays enabled where it finds real magic values.
Short single-purpose patterns read positionally (match[1]); groups are named where a pattern has several consumers, and unused capture groups are already written as non-capturing.
The engineering scripts call GitHub, git and dependency tools one request at a time on purpose: pagination cursors, ordering guarantees and rate limits make concurrent awaits incorrect.
Test doubles implement promise-returning interfaces (the GitHub API and stage runners) and must return promises without awaiting; the override covers only test and fixture files.
These workflow policy files state and test GitHub Actions expression text, which contains literal dollar-brace placeholders in ordinary strings by design.

Component-shape conventions that conflict with the established structure: components are typed arrow constants, typed action objects supply handlers whose names already state the action, and prop spreading forwards complete typed records.
The project compiles JSX with the automatic runtime, so React is deliberately not imported into every component module.
The status regions are layout containers; the suggested output element is phrasing content for calculation results, and swapping it would change layout and the locators the accessibility tests pin.
tsc's noImplicitReturns already proves every path returns, and this rule reports exhaustive switches over closed unions as inconsistent.
Type aliases carry unions, mapped types and the generated contract shapes; requiring interfaces would conflict with the generated contract types.
The rule flags every React prop, DOM and library type; immutability is enforced at the contract boundary by the generated Readonly wire types.
Test doubles created with vi.fn are passed to void callback props and assertions read their calls; returning a value from a mock is intentional and cannot affect production code.
Test fixtures assert the shape of synthetic JSON and mocked values, and the generated validator module asserts shapes its own runtime validators have just proved.
Browser flows, script steps and fixture setup are sequential by design: each step depends on the state the previous one produced.
The generated validator accessor keeps its generic so each call site infers the response type from the endpoint identifier.
The bundler emits the standalone validator declaration files with its own array syntax; generated declarations are not hand-edited.

The audit asks for the `$/...` self-repository action syntax, which actionlint and the repository's own workflow policy do not yet understand; the reviewed `./` form is kept until all three accept it.
The validated generated-contract HTTP adapter owns browser transport; this exact adapter may call fetch while operation-domain and other browser callers must use its validated endpoint boundary.

The absence helper explicitly handles enumeration failure and returns its final bounded empty-result predicate. Conditional use distinguishes proven disappearance from inaccessible Docker state without relying on errexit.
Cleanup already disables errexit; this helper explicitly guards the exact owned anonymous volume identity and returns the actual remove command status, which the caller records as cleanup failure.

Diagnostic retention is best effort during an existing restore failure. Each directory setup step explicitly returns on failure; independent Docker diagnostic attempts are intentionally bounded and tolerated without changing the restore failure.
